free_tier.stated: Per-object caps only, and small: nostr.build free uploads 20 MiB, hard cap 100 MiB, then storage plans 5 GB / $18/yr up to 500 GB / $240/yr. 24242.io: 100 MiB max file, files deleted after 60 days unaccessed. blossom.psbt.me: 1 month hosting, files under 1 MB.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: 24242.io: 100 MiB max file, files deleted after 60 days unaccessed

interface_detail: BUD-01/BUD-06 HTTP API: PUT /upload, HEAD /upload, DELETE; auth is a signed Nostr event in the Authorization header, not an account.
tooling: any Blossom client; curl with a signed event.
chaining: Content-addressed by sha256, so it chunks naturally into the hoangvu12/free-s3 pattern. But 20 MiB chunks would need ~50,000 objects per TiB.
limits_note: 20 MiB free / 100 MiB absolute on nostr.build; 100 MiB on 24242.io; 1 MB on psbt.me. Auth is a signed event, so 'no account' is real: 401 with x-reason 'Missing Blossom Authorization header'.
reliability_note: Cryptographic keypair authentication with no registration required. Hosted blossom instances enforce 60-day idle deletion policies.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

extras.agent_focus: Two client questions. (1) Open academic infrastructure that does NOT validate institutional identity — for each repository I probed the machine-readable quota endpoint (GET /api/dataverses/:root/storage/quota, /api/records?size=1, /api/info/version) rather than trusting marketing pages, and separately tested the write gate, because open-signup-with-unlimited-quota and open-signup-with-deposit-rights are different things and this wave exists to separate them. (2) Relay/P2P, split into signalling (coordinates only) vs relaying (data transits, operator pays). Secondary sweep: the 2025-26 AI data commons (FineWeb, Common Pile, DCLM, Dolma, Pleias) to establish whether any of them offers writable storage — none does; they are all read-only distribution on HF or Common Crawl S3, i.e. egress sources, not deposit targets. Dataverse turns out to be the only architecture in this space that ships a quota API that answers 'is there a limit' in one GET, so I ran it across every instance I could reach.

binding_note: a clock, not a quota: bytes leave whether or not transfer is completed
